newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 3.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 3.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
Westpac Banking Corp Ltd and Bank of Melbourne announced early on Thursday they would merge, with Westpac making an offer through a scheme of arangement valuing Bank of Melbourne at A$1.435 billion.

Lend Lease Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it had sold 15 million shares in Westpac Banking Corp for A$7.00 each, raising A$105 million. It said the profit from the deal would be applied against anticipated writedowns in the valuation of Melbourne's Grant Central property.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$16.69 (+0.17)

The U.S.-Australian development of the giant Bayu-Undan gas field in the Timor Sea cleared its biggest hurdle on Wednesday when BHP Petroleum and Phillips Petroleum agreed that BHP should be the sole operator.Joint venture participants said the agreement meant they could now consider exactly how to develop the A$4 billion field and whether to build a liquified natural gas (LNG) processing plant onshore near Darwin in the Northern Territory or build such a plant offshore.
Coca Cola Amatil announced at its annual meeting that it is due combine its Philippines soft drinks unit with San Miguel.
Foodland due to release its results for the first half of its financial year. It said in February that sales for the 26 weeks to January 26 fell 0.9 percent to A$1.855 billion.

Former Estate Mortgage trust, Meridian Investment Trust, said on Wednesday former Estate Mortgage auditors Priestley & Morris had agreed to pay A$31 million in an out-of-court settlement. Meridian and its managers Tyndall Funds Management ltd are pitted against defendants, including food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co Ltd in the Estate Mortgage case.
